**Step 1 – Quick starter plan** You’re aiming for a simple site where anyone can register, upload a picture of a pet, and others can “like” those photos. That’s an **Amber** project (personal data + uploads + likes). Below is the one‑screen plan with all the safety bits we’ll build in. Ask any of the short questions – they’re just to confirm the details. --- ### 1️⃣ One‑screen plan ``` What we are building: A pet‑photo gallery where users can upload pictures and like each other’s photos. Who uses it: Public (anyone with a browser). Risk level: Amber (logins, personal data, uploads, likes). Day‑one features: 1. User can sign‑up/sign‑in (magic‑link email). 2. Logged‑in user can upload a photo (jpg/png, ≤5 MB). 3. Logged‑in user can view a public feed of photos and tap a heart to like a photo. Information it stores: email (hashed by Supabase), photo files, photo meta (id, user_id, likes count, uploader’s id). All private to the user except the photos themselves in a public feed. Logins: Yes, email‑only magic link via Supabase Auth. Money: No. Built with: Lovable (low‑code builder) + Supabase (database + authentication + storage). Safety: secrets in .env, RLS rules, like limits, upload size limit, per‑user ID checks, retry‑safe commits, and a save point before each change. Not in version 1: comments, comments moderation, payment, advanced AI, admin dashboard. ``` Does that look right? If yes → we’ll start building the first feature. If you want to tweak something (typical for question 1‑3), let me know. --- ### 2️⃣ Quick starter questions (Amber, 3 questions) 1. **Who is it for?** • Just you and a few friends, or open to everyone on the internet? 2. **What must it do on day one?** • Sign‑up, upload a photo, and like photos? Any other must‑have? 3. **What information will it keep?** • Besides photo files – is there any other personal data (name, phone, address)? Your answers help us decide a few small details (e.g., “public feed only” vs “private feed”) and keep the plan concise. --- ### 3️⃣ Safety parts we’ll build in (explained plainly) | Feature | Safety part | |--------|-------------| | **Photo uploads** | • Users can only add, edit, or delete *their own* photos.
• Only JPG/PNG, ≤5 MB.
• Photos live in a private Supabase bucket unless you choose to make the feed public (we’ll set it public so visitors can see the feed, but uploads remain private to the owner). | | **Likes** | • Users can like only *one* photo at a time (prevent “spam” liking).
• Like count stored in a separate, read‑only table that only the owner of the photo can read, so others see the count but not the liker’s identity.
• RLS rules prevent other users from seeing who liked a photo. | | **Logins** | • Supabase Auth magic‑link (email‑only).
• No password, no social logins to keep it simple. | | **Secrets** | • All keys live in a `.env` file *never* in frontend code.
• We’ll use Supabase’s “anon” key for the client and the “service_role” key only on the server (if we need any server‑side APIs). | | **Save points** | • After every step we’ll tag a “save point” (a git commit or a Lovable history snapshot) so you can revert if anything breaks. | --- ### 4️⃣ Next step Once you reply to the questions, I’ll give the exact Lovable screen‑by‑screen instructions (or a code snippet if you’re comfortable) to: 1. **Create the Supabase project** (if you don’t have one yet). 2. **Add the Auth magic‑link and set up the email domain.** 3. **Create the photos table & storage bucket with RLS rules.** 4. **Build the upload UI** with file‑type and size checks. 5. **Build the feed and like button** with the RLS‑protected like table. I’ll also show you how to **save‑point** after each change so you’ll always have a working copy. Let me know your answers (or if you’d like us to go straight to step 1 – just say “no questions, start the build”).
